questions.mapArea: Language: Understand, Edit for Grammar, Usage
questions.stem: A compound subject is two or more subjects joined by a word such as and. Which sentence has a compound subject?
options: Reem painted the sea and hung up the picture.
Reem painted a big blue picture of the sea.
Reem painted the sea with her new brushes.
Reem and Dana painted a picture of the sea.
questions.why: Reem and Dana are two subjects joined by and, so together they are a compound subject.

questions.why: Two people joined by and make a plural subject, so the verb is play.

questions.why: The cat and the kitten are two animals. Subjects joined by and take a plural verb: sleep.

The dates and the figs taste sweet.
questions.why: Dates and figs joined by and are plural, so the verb is taste (no -s).

questions.passage: (1) The Reading Club meets every Tuesday after school. (2) Kalila and Dimna are the book we are reading this month. (3) Each boy and girl in the club takes a turn reading aloud. (4) Either the club leader or the members choose the next book. (5) The leader, together with her assistants, keep a list of new words.
questions.stem: Which is the correct way to write sentence 5?
options: The leader, together with her assistants, keep a list of new words.
The leader, together with her assistants, keeps a list of new words.
The leader and her assistants keeps a list of new words.
The leader, together with her assistants, are keeping a list of new words.
questions.why: Together with her assistants is extra information. The leader is singular → keeps.

questions.mapArea: Language: Understand, Edit for Grammar, Usage

(4) Either the club leader or the members choose the next book. (5) The leader, together with her assistants, keep a list of new words.
questions.stem: Which two sentences of the paragraph about the club use the correct verb? Choose two.
questions.why: Sentence 3: each + compound → takes. Sentence 4: either…or, members is closer → choose. Sentences 2 and 5 need is and keeps.

questions.passage: (1) My uncle and his family love history. (2) Last spring, not only my cousins but also my uncle were eager to see the old tombs at Hegra. (3) Each rock and carving ____ a story about people who lived long ago. (4) Our guide, as well as the signs near each site, explains what the carvings mean. (5) Neither the heat nor the long walks bothers my little cousin.
questions.stem: Which change corrects the verb in sentence 2 about the trip?
questions.why: With not only…but also, the verb agrees with the closer subject. My uncle is singular → was.

questions.stem: How should sentence 5 be corrected?
options: Neither the heat nor the long walks bother my little cousin.
Neither the heat nor the long walk bother my little cousin.
Neither the heat or the long walks bothers my little cousin.
Neither the heat nor the long walks is bothering my little cousin.
questions.why: Walks is closer to the verb and is plural, so the verb is bother.

questions.stem: Choose the verb that correctly completes sentence 3.
questions.why: Each before a compound subject means one at a time, so the verb is singular: tells.

questions.stem: True or false: In the sentence “Ten minutes of reading and a short quiz are planned for each lesson,” the verb are is correct.
questions.why: Ten minutes of reading and a short quiz are two things joined by and, so the plural verb are is correct.

questions.stem: Which verb correctly completes the sentence? “Beside the old well ____ a palm tree and a small stone bench.”
questions.why: The subject comes after the verb: a palm tree and a small stone bench. Joined by and, it is plural → stand.

questions.stem: Find and fix the verb that does not agree with its subject in this sentence about the instructions.
segments: clear enough for the new students.
questions.why: Example is closer to the verb and is singular, so the verb is was.

questions.mapArea: Language: Understand, Edit for Grammar, Usage
questions.stem: Which sentence about the schedule is written correctly?
options: Every student and teacher were given a copy of the schedule.
The students, along with a teacher, was given the schedule.
Not only the teacher but also the students was given it.
Every student and teacher was given a copy of the schedule.
questions.why: Every + a compound subject takes a singular verb. In the last two, students is the subject that decides the verb, so it must be were.

questions.mapArea: Language: Understand, Edit for Grammar, Usage
questions.stem: In which sentence does the compound subject name one thing, so the verb is singular?
options: Bread and butter is my brother’s favorite snack.
Bread and juice are on the kitchen table.
The bread and the butter are in the fridge.
Butter and jam are good on warm bread.
questions.why: Bread and butter here is one snack (buttered bread), so it takes is. In the others, two separate things take are.

questions.mapArea: Language: Understand, Edit for Grammar, Usage
questions.stem: Which sentence best combines these two sentences? “Hessa is planning the party. Her sisters are planning the party too.”
options: Hessa and her sisters is planning the party.
Hessa, as well as her sisters, are planning it.
Hessa and her sisters are planning the party.
Either Hessa or her sisters is planning it.
questions.why: Joined by and, Hessa and her sisters is a plural subject → are. With as well as, the verb would have to be is.
